column2: Bassist Aaron Bell anchored Duke Ellington's orchestra in 1960-62, including the 'Nutcracker Suite', then worked as an arranger and jazz educator.
Jazz pianist Aaron Goldberg's trio with Reuben Rogers and Eric Harland made 'Worlds' (2006), featuring guests Luciana Souza and Kurt Rosenwinkel.
Pianist Aaron Parks recorded 'Find the Way' with bassist Ben Street and drummer Billy Hart in October 2015; ECM released the lyrical trio set in 2017.
Clarinetist Aaron Sachs formed the Manor Re-Bops in 1946 and recorded Clarinet and Co. in 1957 with Jimmy Raney, Hall Overton and Osie Johnson.
Free-jazz cellist Abdul Wadud recorded the solo album 'By Myself' (1977); his cello also shaped Julius Hemphill's 'Dogon A.D.' (1972).
South African pianist (1934-2026) mixed jazz and Cape rhythms. 'Mannenberg' (1974) became an anti-apartheid anthem; worked with Duke Ellington; played Mandela's 1994 inauguration.
Swing clarinetist Abe Most joined Les Brown in 1939 and played with Tommy Dorsey in 1946 before becoming a busy Los Angeles studio musician.
Pianist Achim Kaufmann co-led 'Pith & Twig' (2014) with bassist Robert Landfermann and drummer Christian Lillinger in the experimental trio gruenen.
Dutch flugelhorn player Ack van Rooyen co-founded the United Jazz + Rock Ensemble and played in Gil Evans's and Peter Herbolzheimer's orchestras.
Keyboardist Adam Holzman performed with Miles Davis in 1985-89, serving as musical director during Davis's late electric-jazz period.
Jazz vocalist whose wordless style shaped early swing. Recorded 'Creole Love Call' and 'The Blues I Love to Sing' with Duke Ellington's orchestra in October 1927.
Japanese pianist and vocalist Akiko Yano made her solo debut with Japanese Girl in 1976 and later collaborated with Yellow Magic Orchestra and the duo yanokami.
Guitarist Al Di Meola joined Chick Corea's Return to Forever in 1974, recording 'Romantic Warrior' (1976) before a solo jazz-fusion career including 'Elegant Gypsy'.
Soul/gospel singer Al Green released 'Back Up Train' with the Soul Mates in 1967 (R&B hit in 1968); later shaped Hi Records' Memphis sound with Willie Mitchell.
Bebop pianist Al Haig recorded with Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker in the 1940s and joined Miles Davis's early 'Birth of the Cool' sessions.
Bassist Al Lucas recorded Boneology and Down Vernon's Alley with J.J. Johnson, Leo Parker, Hank Jones and Shadow Wilson for Savoy in New York on Dec. 24, 1947.
Tenor saxophonist Al Sears joined Duke Ellington's orchestra in 1944, played on its 1945 It Don't Mean a Thing remake and recorded Swingville leader albums in 1960.
Clarinetist and tenor saxophonist Alan Greenspan played in Henry Jerome's New York swing band (1944-45), long before his career as Federal Reserve chairman.
British saxophonist Alan Wakeman worked with Paul Lytton and Harry Miller before performing with Mike Westbrook, Graham Collier and Soft Machine.
Blues/jazz singer (1895-1984), Harlem Renaissance star. Recorded 'How Long, Sweet Daddy, How Long?' (1921); sang with King Oliver at Chicago's Dreamland Cafe; toured Europe 1927.
Saxophonist Pee Wee Ellis arranged and co-wrote James Brown's 'Cold Sweat' and 'Licking Stick', bringing jazz horns into the foundations of funk.
Swedish singer Alice Babs was a featured soloist in Duke Ellington's Second Sacred Concert in New York in 1968 and Third Sacred Concert in London in 1973.
French clarinetist and tenor saxophonist Alix Combelle recorded 'Crazy Rhythm' in Paris in August 1935 with the Quintette du Hot Club de France.
Fusion drummer Alphonse Mouzon played on Weather Report's debut and became a member of Larry Coryell's Eleventh House in the mid-1970s.
Trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire's 2020 Blue Note quartet album 'on the tender spot of every calloused moment' reimagines the blues with Sam Harris and Harish Raghavan.
Israeli-born jazz clarinetist Anat Cohen blends swing with Brazilian choro; 'Rosa Dos Ventos' pairs her with Trio Brasileiro on choro-inspired music.
Romanian vocalist Anca Parghel recorded the Klaus Ignatzek Trio album Airballoon in the Netherlands in March and April 1992.
Norwegian pianist Anders Aarum debuted his trio on Lucky Strike in 2000 and recorded Oslo Puzzle with Jens Fossum and Hermund Nygard in 2023.
Norwegian pianist Andreas Ulvo made Eple Trio's debut 'Made This' (2007) with bassist Sigurd Hole and drummer Jonas Sjovaag, drawing on Scandinavian jazz.
Jazz pianist Andy LaVerne studied with Bill Evans, toured with Stan Getz and recorded Four Miles with Randy Brecker, George Mraz and Al Foster.
Steelpan jazz musician Andy Narell released his first leader album in 1979 and developed calypso-inspired improvisation and music for large steel bands.
Saxophonist Angelika Niescier led 'The Berlin Concert' (2017) with Christopher Tordini on bass and Tyshawn Sorey on drums; Intakt issued it in 2018.
Singer Anita O'Day worked with Gene Krupa and Stan Kenton, then made influential Verve albums; her 1958 Newport performance became a jazz-film highlight.
German pianist Anke Helfrich recorded We'll Rise with Dietmar Fuhr, Jens Duppe and guest trombonist Adrian Mears, portraying pioneering women through jazz.
Dutch singer Ann Burton recorded Blue Burton in 1967 with Louis van Dijk, Jacques Schols, John Engels and Piet Noordijk; Artone issued it first.
French drummer Anne Paceo composed 'Bright Shadows' (2019), joining Christophe Panzani's saxophone, Pierre Perchaud's guitar and Tony Paeleman's keys.
Dutch trombonist Annemarie Roelofs explored microtonal improvisation with ten-string guitarist Pascal Marzan on Berlin & London, issued in 2026.
Jazz vocalist Annie Ross recorded 'Twisted' in 1952, setting her own words to Wardell Gray's saxophone solo; she later joined Lambert, Hendricks & Ross.
British trombonist Annie Whitehead began with Ivy Benson's all-woman orchestra, later played jazz with Working Week and led her own 1984 album 'Mix Up'.
Keyboard improviser Anthony Coleman led Sephardic Tinge on three Tzadik albums (1995-2002), exploring Jewish musical traditions in downtown jazz.
Pianist-composer Anthony Davis built the flexible Episteme ensemble around composed and improvised music, later carrying its players into opera.
Jazz guitarist Anthony Wilson accompanied Diana Krall at Paris's Olympia on Nov. 29-Dec. 2, 2001, on Live in Paris, issued by Verve in 2002.
Tenor saxophonist Archie Shepp recorded 'Attica Blues' in 1972, using large-ensemble soul and gospel colors to address the Attica prison uprising.
Chicago saxophonist Ari Brown joined the AACM in 1971 and led his Delmark debut 'Ultimate Frontier' in 1995, linking spiritual and avant-garde jazz.
Drummer Ari Hoenig led the 2008 album 'Bert's Playground'; his Punk Bop group was joined by Chris Potter and guitarist Jonathan Kreisberg.
Alto saxophonist Arthur Blythe's 'Lenox Avenue Breakdown' (1979) mixes free jazz and funk with tuba, flute and guitar; the septet includes James Blood Ulmer.
Clarinetist (1910-2004) led a swing orchestra that recorded 'Begin the Beguine' in 1938; his band briefly featured Billie Holiday, and he later performed at Carnegie Hall.
Cuban trumpeter Arturo Sandoval, mentored by Dizzy Gillespie, combines Afro-Cuban jazz phrasing and virtuoso trumpet playing with classical repertoire.
Hungarian jazz guitarist Attila Zoller recorded Gypsy Cry with Herbie Hancock in 1969 and a final 1998 trio session with Tommy Flanagan and George Mraz.
Hamburg-born boogie-woogie pianist Axel Zwingenberger began recording in 1976 and recorded with Big Joe Turner in Los Angeles in May 1978.
Azerbaijani pianist and singer Aziza Mustafa Zadeh recorded Always in 1993 with John Patitucci and Dave Weckl and Dance of Fire in 1995.
Brazilian guitarist and vocalist Badi Assad recorded 'Solo' (1994) for Chesky; her percussive guitar and voice cross Brazilian music, classical technique and jazz.
Australian pianist Barney McAll co-founded Groove Collective after moving to New York in the 1990s and released the leader albums Mooroolbark and Hearing the Blood.
Double bassist Barre Phillips recorded 'End To End' (2018), a solo ECM album of spontaneous acoustic improvisations informed by decades of free jazz.
Drummer Barrett Deems played in Louis Armstrong's band in the 1950s and appears on 'Satch Plays Fats' and 'Louis Armstrong Plays W. C. Handy'.
Guitarist Ben Monder's ECM album 'Amorphae' pairs atmospheric guitar with drummers Paul Motian and Andrew Cyrille in open, textural improvisation.
Drummer Ben Riley played in Thelonious Monk's quartet in 1964-67 and later worked with Alice Coltrane, Ron Carter and the Monk-focused group Sphere.
Norwegian saxophonist Bendik Hofseth plays on Oystein Sevag's Caravan, recorded in Germany and Oslo during 2004 and 2005.
Trumpeter Benny Bailey played with Gillespie's and Hampton's big bands; his Candid LP 'Big Brass' (1960 session) features Phil Woods and Julius Watkins.
Tenor saxophonist/composer (1929-2024) wrote 'I Remember Clifford' and 'Killer Joe'; played with Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers and founded the Jazztet with Art Farmer.
Swing trombonist Benny Morton played with Fletcher Henderson in the late 1920s and joined Count Basie in 1937, remaining until 1940.
Trombonist Benny Powell played the bridge on Count Basie's hit 'April in Paris'; his bold tenor and bass trombone sound connected swing to bebop.
Dutch trombonist Bert Boeren recorded live in The Hague on June 21, 2024 with Four Others and previously played in the Dutch Swing College Band from 1985 to 1999.
Tuba player Bill Barber performed with Miles Davis's nonet on the 1949-50 Birth of the Cool recordings and later appeared on Miles Ahead and Porgy and Bess.
Drummer Bill Bruford led the jazz-rock band Bruford on 'Feels Good to Me' (1978), with guitarist Allan Holdsworth and keyboardist Dave Stewart.
Trumpeter Bill Chase led the brass-heavy jazz-rock band Chase. Their hit 'Get It On' (1971) featured a four-trumpet section plus organ, guitar, bass and drums.
Bassist Bill Crow joined Gerry Mulligan's sextet in 1954, playing with Zoot Sims and Bob Brookmeyer in a long association with Mulligan.
Bassist/producer Bill Laswell's Material project released 'Hallucination Engine' (1994), mixing jazz improvisation, dub grooves and Indian music.
Jazz guitarist Billy Bauer played on Lennie Tristano's 1949 'Intuition' session with Lee Konitz and Warne Marsh, opening space for collective improvisation.
Fusion drummer Billy Cobham propelled Mahavishnu Orchestra, then led 'Spectrum' (1973), merging intricate jazz rhythms with rock, funk and Jan Hammer's keyboards.
Singer and bandleader Billy Eckstine formed a groundbreaking bebop big band in 1944, with Dizzy Gillespie as music director and Charlie Parker leading the saxes.
Drummer Billy Hart recorded ECM's 'All Our Reasons' (2012) with Ethan Iverson, Mark Turner and Ben Street, balancing rhythmic swing and abstraction.
Drummer Billy Higgins brought supple swing to Ornette Coleman's 1959 quartet; his sensitive drumming later supported countless hard-bop Blue Note sessions.
Singer Bing Crosby was one of Paul Whiteman's Rhythm Boys singing on the Feb. 18, 1928 Victor 21274 recording of Mississippi Mud with the jazz-age orchestra.
Cornetist (1903-1931) famed for lyrical early-jazz solos. Hear 'Singin' the Blues' (1927), recorded in New York with Frankie Trumbauer's orchestra.
Bandleader Blanche Calloway launched the Joy Boys in 1931; her touring orchestra and swing recordings broke barriers for Black women directing bands.
New Orleans blues singer Blue Lu Barker recorded Don't You Feel My Leg in 1938, worked alongside guitarist Danny Barker and made a final live recording at Jazz Fest in 1998.
Tenor saxophonist Bob Berg played in Miles Davis's electric band in 1984-86 after work with Horace Silver, Chick Corea and Cedar Walton.
Baritone saxophonist Bob Gordon recorded 'Meet Mr. Gordon' in Los Angeles in May 1954 with arranger Jack Montrose, a West Coast chamber-jazz session.
Flautist Bobbi Humphrey made the 1973 Blue Note crossover album Blacks and Blues with Larry and Fonce Mizell's jazz-funk production.
Cornetist Bobby Hackett's lyrical solo on Glenn Miller's 'A String of Pearls' (recorded 1941) gave the swing hit a delicate New Orleans-jazz color.
Brazilian guitarist Bola Sete recorded Mambossa with Vince Guaraldi, Fred Marshall and Jerry Granelli in 1963 and played on Guaraldi's Live at El Matador.
Bandleader Boyd Raeburn led a racially mixed, bebop-oriented big band from 1942 to 1949 with musicians including Roy Eldridge, Dizzy Gillespie and Oscar Pettiford.
Los Angeles trombonist Britt Woodman worked with Les Hite and Boyd Raeburn before joining Duke Ellington, who featured him on the Such Sweet Thunder suite.
Jazz pianist Bruce Barth worked with Stanley Turrentine and Terence Blanchard after moving to New York in 1988; his trio recorded live at the Village Vanguard.
Jazz drummer Bruce Ditmas led the 1995 Postcards album What If with John Abercrombie, Paul Bley, Dominic Richards and Sam Rivers; he wrote its title track.
Jazz guitarist Bruce Forman leads the western-bebop band Cow Bop and recorded soundtrack performances for three Clint Eastwood films, including Million Dollar Baby.
Swiss saxophonist Bruno Spoerri began electronic experiments in 1965 and co-founded the Swiss Society for Computer Music in 1982.
Italian bassist Bruno Tommaso recorded Blues Waltz in Rome in October 1990 with pianist Gianni Lenoci and drummer Antonio Di Lorenzo.
Trumpeter Buck Clayton joined Count Basie in 1936; his solo on 'Fiesta in Blue' and arrangements such as 'Taps Miller' shaped classic swing.
Washington tenor saxophonist Buck Hill recorded Capital Hill at Van Gelder Studio in 1989 with pianist Barry Harris, bassist Ray Drummond and drummer Freddie Waits.
Guitarist Bucky Pizzarelli performed in The Tonight Show band during the 1960s and 1970s, toured with Benny Goodman and recorded with veteran swing players including Zoot Sims.
Tenor saxophonist Budd Johnson worked with Louis Armstrong and Earl Hines in the 1930s and helped organize early bebop sessions in New York.
Trumpeter Buddy Childers joined Stan Kenton's big band as lead trumpet in 1942 at just 16, later playing and writing for other major jazz orchestras.
Berlin percussionist Burkhard Beins joined Polwechsel in 2004; the quartet's Traces of Wood features member-composed pieces and electroacoustic improvisation.
Pianist Burton Greene formed the Free Form Improvisation Ensemble with Alan Silva in 1963 and joined the Jazz Composers Guild the next year.
Free-jazz bassist Buschi Niebergall played on Globe Unity Orchestra's 'Live in Wuppertal', recorded March 25, 1973, with Evan Parker and Peter Kowald.
Trombonist Buster Cooper played with Lionel Hampton and in the Apollo Theater house band before serving in Duke Ellington's orchestra from 1962 to 1969.
Kansas City alto saxophonist Buster Smith mentored Charlie Parker and co-led a Band of Rhythm with Count Basie, shaping the Texas sax sound.
Bassist Buster Williams played in Herbie Hancock's Mwandishi sextet, appearing on 'Mwandishi' (1971), 'Crossings' (1972) and 'Sextant' (1973).
Swing drummer Butch Ballard toured Europe with Duke Ellington in 1950, played with Count Basie and worked with Cootie Williams at Harlem's Savoy Ballroom.
Drummer Butch Miles played in Count Basie's orchestra in 1975-79 and 1997-2007, carrying the forceful swing pulse of big-band jazz.
Cornetist Butch Morris devised 'Conduction', directing large improvising ensembles through gestures rather than fixed written scores.
Singer and bandleader Cab Calloway recorded 'Minnie the Moocher' (1931); its dramatic vocal performance entered the US National Recording Registry in 2018.
Afro-Cuban bassist Cachao and brother Orestes helped create mambo in 1937; he brought jazz-style jam sessions into Cuban dance music in 1957.
Trumpeter-composer Cal Massey wrote Bakai for John Coltrane and Cry of My People for Archie Shepp; his compositions were also recorded by Lee Morgan and Jackie McLean.
Guitarist Calvin Newborn recorded Atlantic's Here Is Phineas on May 3, 1956 with pianist Phineas Newborn Jr., bassist Oscar Pettiford and drummer Kenny Clarke.
Bassist Cameron Brown recorded Here and How! in Brussels in November 1997 with Dave Ballou, Leon Parker, Sheila Jordan and guest Dewey Redman.
Dutch saxophonist Candy Dulfer began leading a band at 13; her 1990 solo debut Saxuality received a Grammy nomination.
Trombonist Carl Fontana's solo on Stan Kenton's 'Intermission Riff' showed a nimble, expressive trombone voice; he also played with Woody Herman.
Swing guitarist Carl Kress developed an elaborate chordal acoustic style, played with Paul Whiteman in 1926 and recorded guitar duets with Eddie Lang.
Norwegian bassist Carl Morten Iversen recorded Trio '87 with pianist Armen Donelian and drummer Audun Kleive in Oslo on July 11, 1987; all three co-wrote Song With No Name.
Trumpeter Carl Saunders worked with Stan Kenton in 1961-62, joined Bill Holman's Los Angeles orchestra in 1984 and led Bebop Big Band on Sea Breeze.
Composer and bandleader (1936-2023) shaped avant-garde jazz with 'Escalator over the Hill'; worked with Michael Mantler and Charlie Haden and toured Europe and Japan.
Electric bassist Carles Benavent joined Paco de Lucia's sextet in 1981 and worked with Chick Corea on 'Touchstone' (1982), connecting jazz and flamenco.
British drummer Carlo Krahmer led a January 11, 1948 London Esquire session with Humphrey Lyttelton and Wally Fawkes, recording That Da Da Strain.
Portuguese flutist Carlos Bechegas recorded Open Secrets with Peter Kowald in 2001 and Secrets Under Trees with Ernesto and Guilherme Rodrigues in 2023.
Brazilian bossa nova composer Carlos Lyra introduced Primavera to Paul Winter after the 1962 Carnegie Hall concert; Winter later recorded the song.
Panama-born alto saxophonist and flutist Carlos Ward played on Don Cherry's Relativity Suite and worked with Abdullah Ibrahim and Cecil Taylor.
Portuguese violinist Carlos Zingaro recorded the improvising trio Trizmaris in Lisbon in March 2023 with bassist Joao Madeira and drummer Sofia Borges.
Trumpeter Carmell Jones played on Horace Silver's 'Song for My Father' (1964) with Joe Henderson, Teddy Smith and Roger Humphries before moving to Berlin.
Jazz vocalist-composer Carmen Lundy debuted with 'Good Morning Kiss' (1985) and recorded 'Modern Ancestors' (2019) and 'Fade to Black' (2022).
Rhythm guitarist Carmen Mastren worked with Tommy Dorsey in 1936-40 and recorded with Sidney Bechet and Muggsy Spanier in 1940, later joining Glenn Miller's Army band.
Singer/pianist (1920-1994) brought subtle phrasing to jazz ballads. Sang with Benny Carter and Count Basie; recorded 'Carmen Sings Monk' (1988) and played Montreux.
Chicago jazz violinist-bandleader Carroll Dickerson led Sunset Cafe orchestras joined by Louis Armstrong and Earl Hines in the 1920s.
Bassist Carson Smith joined the pianoless Gerry Mulligan quartet with Chet Baker in 1952, later playing in small groups led by Russ Freeman and Chico Hamilton.
Danish pianist Carsten Dahl recorded Painting Music in 2019 with bassist Nils Bo Davidsen and drummer Stefan Pasborg, releasing the trio project on ACT.
Clarinetist and tenor saxophonist Castor McCord recorded Dinah and Tiger Rag with Louis Armstrong's orchestra for OKeh in New York on May 4, 1930.
Trumpeter Cat Anderson joined Duke Ellington in 1944, left to lead a band in 1947-49, and was noted for precise, brilliant high-register solos.
Swing vocalist Catherine Russell recorded Send For Me with guitarist-director Matt Munisteri, bassist Tal Ronen and drummer Mark McLean for Dot Time in 2022.
Bassist Cecil McBee led 'Mutima' (recorded May 1974), bringing African-influenced rhythms and searching modal improvisation to Strata-East jazz.
Clarinetist and saxophonist Cecil Scott played on Teddy Wilson's February 18, 1937 New York Brunswick session backing Billie Holiday on The Mood That I'm In.
Pianist Cedar Walton wrote 'Mosaic' and 'Ugetsu' for Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers, then co-founded Eastern Rebellion with Clifford Jordan in 1974.
Brazilian guitarist and songwriter Celso Fonseca collaborated on albums with lyricist Ronaldo Bastos and recorded Pagina Central with Marcos Valle in 2009.
Drummer Chad Wackerman toured and recorded with Frank Zappa for seven years and worked extensively with guitarist Allan Holdsworth, including eight albums.
Singer Chaka Khan performed jazz standards on 'Echoes of an Era' (1982) with Joe Henderson, Freddie Hubbard, Chick Corea, Stanley Clarke and Lenny White.
Jazz pianist and singer Champian Fulton recorded Meet Me at Birdland live in September 2022 with Hide Tanaka and Fukushi Tainaka.
Cuban conga player (1915-1948) joined Dizzy Gillespie; they performed at Carnegie Hall in 1947 and recorded 'Manteca', bringing Afro-Cuban rhythms into modern jazz.
St. Louis drummer Charles Bobo Shaw co-founded the Black Artists Group and led the Human Arts Ensemble, joining free jazz energy to funk rhythms.
Organist Charles Kynard combined soul jazz with electric bass playing; he recorded Where It's At for Pacific Jazz in 1963 and Afro-Disiac for Prestige in 1970.
Belgian pianist Charles Loos co-founded the Loos-Lazarevitch International Quintet and recorded with Eric Legnini, Steve Houben and Maurane.
Alto saxophonist Charles McPherson recorded 'Bebop Revisited!' with pianist Barry Harris and trumpeter Carmell Jones on November 20, 1964.
Drummer Charles Moffett played in Ornette Coleman's trio with David Izenzon during 1965-67 and recorded with Archie Shepp on Four for Trane.
New Orleans saxophonist Charles Neville played in the Dew Drop Inn house band, joined the Neville Brothers and lent saxophone to Yellow Moon.
Trumpeter Charles Tolliver and pianist Stanley Cowell founded Strata-East in 1971 after recording the Music Inc. big band, championing artist-owned jazz.
Baritone saxophonist Charles Tyler worked with Albert Ayler on Bells and Spirits Rejoice before making free-jazz leader dates for ESP-Disk.
Baritone saxophonist Charlie Fowlkes joined Count Basie's band in 1953 after playing with Lionel Hampton, anchoring the saxophone section's low voice.
Bassist Charlie Haden (1937-2014) played on Ornette Coleman's 'The Shape of Jazz to Come' (1959); founded the Liberation Music Orchestra with Carla Bley in 1969.
Alto saxophonist Charlie Holmes joined Luis Russell in 1928; he later played in Louis Armstrong's backing band and with Cootie Williams.
Jazz-funk guitarist Charlie Hunter played bass lines and melodies at once on his custom eight-string guitar; hear the 1995 trio album 'Bing, Bing, Bing!'.
Tenor saxophonist Charlie Rouse brought a dry, melodic bop tone to Thelonious Monk's quartet from 1959-70; earlier he co-led the Jazz Modes.
Trumpeter Charlie Shavers arranged for John Kirby's agile swing sextet and co-wrote the jazz standard 'Undecided', first popular in 1939.
Trumpeter Charlie Teagarden recorded Beale Street Blues with Eddie Lang and Joe Venuti's All-Stars in 1931 and joined Paul Whiteman's band in 1933.
Tenor saxophonist Charlie Ventura played with Gene Krupa and founded 'Bop for the People' in 1946, taking accessible bebop arrangements to dance audiences.
Drummer Charlie Watts led a jazz quintet on 'A Tribute to Charlie Parker with Strings' (1992), featuring saxophonist Peter King and bassist Dave Green.
Swiss drummer Charly Antolini worked with Sidney Bechet and Albert Nicholas in Paris, then played with Benny Goodman, Earl Hines and Art Farmer.
Drummer Ches Smith led We All Break on 'Path of Seven Colors' (2021), combining Haitian Vodou drumming and jazz improvisation with pianist Matt Mitchell.
Guitarists Chet Atkins and Les Paul revisited jazz standards including 'Caravan' on their 1976 duet album 'Chester & Lester', crossing country and jazz guitar.
Tenor saxophonist Chico Freeman recorded 'Spirit Sensitive' (1978-79) with pianist John Hicks, bassist Cecil McBee and drummer Billy Hart.
Cuban composer Chico O'Farrill orchestrated Afro Cuban Jazz Suite in 1950 for an ensemble involving Machito, Charlie Parker and Buddy Rich.
Vocalist China Forbes joined Pink Martini in 1995 and co-wrote and sang Sympathique with pianist Thomas Lauderdale on their 1997 Heinz Records debut album.
Chromatic harmonica player Chris Bauer performs bop, ballads and Latin jazz standards. His album 'In A Yuletide Groove' interprets seasonal songs in a swing style.
British saxophonist and alto clarinetist Chris Biscoe played in Didier Levallet's Orchestre National de Jazz on Sequences, recorded in 1999.
Tenor saxophonist Chris Cheek recorded 'I Wish I Knew' in 1996-97 with guitarist Kurt Rosenwinkel, bassist Chris Higgins and drummer Jorge Rossy.
Swing guitarist Chris Flory recorded City Life for Concord in 1993 with John Bunch, John Webber and Chuck Riggs after years in Scott Hamilton's group.
Belgian percussionist Chris Joris recorded Until the Darkness Fades live in Mechelen with violin, cello and guest saxophone, blending improvisation and chamber music.
Bassist Chris Laurence played on Kenny Wheeler's Songs for Quintet, recorded at Abbey Road in December 2013 with Stan Sulzmann, John Parricelli and Martin France.
Pianist Chris McGregor led the multiracial South African Blue Notes and, in exile, Brotherhood of Breath, joining township rhythms to free jazz.
British trombonist Chris Pyne recorded John Surman's The Brass Project in London in April 1992 and appears on Kenny Wheeler's 1990 ECM large-ensemble album.
Bassist Chris White played on the 1967 New York sessions for Jimmy Owens and Kenny Barron's Atlantic quintet album You Had Better Listen, with Benny Maupin on reeds.
Memphis-born alto saxophonist Chris Woods first recorded as a leader for United in 1952, later played with Clark Terry and recorded Modus Operandi for Delmark in 1978.
Drummer Christian Lillinger's 'Open Form for Society' (2019) linked chamber-like ensemble composition, dense rhythms, keyboards and free-jazz energy.
Austrian trombonist and composer Christian Muthspiel leads Orjazztra Vienna, whose albums include Homecoming (2022) and La Melodia della Strada (2023).
German reed player and composer Christina Fuchs co-leads FUCHSTHONE ORCHESTRA and records small-group work with accordionist Florian Stadler as FLUX.
Bassist Chubby Jackson played with Woody Herman and won the 1947 Down Beat bassist poll; he advocated a five-string upright bass for jazz.
Stride pianist Cliff Jackson recorded Horse Feathers and The Terror with his Krazy Kats in 1930 and later worked with Sidney Bechet in 1940-41.
Berlin jazz guitarist Coco Schumann joined the Ghetto Swingers in Theresienstadt in 1943, survived Auschwitz and continued performing jazz after the war.
Tenor saxophonist (1904-1969) helped establish the instrument in jazz. His celebrated 'Body and Soul' solo was recorded in New York in 1939 with Gene Rodgers and others.
Singer Connee Boswell sang lead in the Boswell Sisters, who recorded regularly from 1930 and appeared in The Big Broadcast in 1932; she continued solo after 1936.
West Coast bop trumpeter Conte Candoli played with Woody Herman, Stan Kenton, Howard Rumsey and Shelly Manne, and joined Supersax in the 1970s.
Pittsburgh singer Dakota Staton signed with Capitol in 1954 and won DownBeat's newcomer honor in 1955; her 1957 debut album The Late, Late Show reached the pop charts.
Former tenor saxophonist Dannie Richmond switched to drums in 1955 and joined Charles Mingus; later he worked with Mingus Dynasty and the Adams-Pullen quartet.
Jazz guitarist Dave Stryker played with Stanley Turrentine and Jack McDuff; his 2024 Groove Street paired his organ trio with saxophonist Bob Mintzer.
Cellist David Darling recorded Cycles at Talent Studio in Oslo in November 1981 with Collin Walcott, Steve Kuhn, Jan Garbarek, Arild Andersen and Oscar Castro-Neves.
Guitarist David Torn mixed ambient textures and jazz-rock on 'Cloud About Mercury' (1987), recording with Mark Isham, Tony Levin and Bill Bruford.
Vocalist Dee Dee Bridgewater's 'Red Earth: A Malian Journey' grew from 2006 Bamako sessions with Malian musicians, joining jazz voice to local traditions.
British guitarist Derek Bailey's solo album 'Solo Guitar' (recorded 1971) reshaped free improvisation with fractured phrases and non-tonal guitar textures.
Belgian pianist Diederik Wissels recorded the vocal chamber-jazz EP Sleepless with Ana Rocha and reed player Nicolas Kummert in November 2023.
Austrian pianist and conductor Dieter Glawischnig conducted the NDR Hannover orchestra for John Taylor's 1987 studio suite Quintessence.
Trumpeter Doc Cheatham backed blues singers in vaudeville during the 1920s, toured Europe with Sam Wooding and played lead trumpet with Cab Calloway in the 1930s.
Clarinetist Don Byron produced and arranged Bug Music, recorded at Master Sound in May 1996 with players including Kenny Davis, Uri Caine and Joey Baron.
Jazz harpist Dorothy Ashby recorded The Jazz Harpist in 1957 and Hip Harp in 1958 with Frank Wess; her 1968 Afro-Harping expanded jazz harp into soul.
Duke Ellington's orchestra recorded Billy Strayhorn's 'Take the A Train' for Victor in February 1941; Ray Nance's trumpet solo became part of its identity.
Alto saxophonist Earl Bostic had an R&B chart hit with 'Flamingo' (1951) on King Records; his 1952 band featured a young John Coltrane on tenor sax.
Free-jazz drummer Ed Blackwell played with Ornette Coleman, Don Cherry and Charlie Haden on 1960 Atlantic sessions for 'This Is Our Music'.
Trumpeter Eddie Gale played on Cecil Taylor's Unit Structures and recorded the Blue Note leader albums Ghetto Music (1968) and Black Rhythm Happening (1969).
Jazz guitarist Eddie Lang (1902-1933) recorded with blues guitarist Lonnie Johnson in New York in 1927 and 1929, helping establish jazz guitar as a solo voice.
Brazilian singer and composer Edu Lobo recorded Cantiga de Longe in Los Angeles in 1970 with Hermeto Pascoal and Airto Moreira among the guests.
Brazilian pianist Eliane Elias recorded with Steps Ahead in 1983, then began her own bandleader career in 1986, linking Brazilian and jazz piano styles.
Norwegian jazz vocalist Elin Rosseland composed and sang the 2013 Trondheim Jazz Orchestra album Ekko, drawing on a large ensemble led by Erlend Skomsvoll.
Tenor saxophonist Eric Alexander played in One for All on 'Live at Smoke Vol. 1' (2001) with Jim Rotondi and Steve Davis.
French trumpeter Erik Truffaz recorded 'Bending New Corners' in April 1999 with Patrick Muller, Marcello Giuliani and Marc Erbetta, fusing jazz and beats.
Neo-soul singer Erykah Badu sang 'Afro Blue' on Robert Glasper Experiment's 'Black Radio' (2012), bridging jazz standards, R&B and hip-hop.
Bassist-vocalist Esperanza Spalding joined Terri Lyne Carrington and Leo Genovese for Chamber Music Society, blending improvised jazz with strings in 2010.
Soul and jazz singer Esther Phillips recorded the Kudu album 'From a Whisper to a Scream' in late 1971 with Hank Crawford, Eric Gale and Bernard Purdie.
Mexican pianist and composer Eugenio Toussaint recorded Oinos in 2008 with bassist Eddie Gomez and drummer Gabriel Puentes, after leading Sacbe.
Nigerian saxophonist and bandleader Femi Kuti founded Positive Force in 1986, carrying Afrobeat's jazz and funk rhythms into his own politically charged repertoire.
Gambian kora player Foday Musa Suso played on Herbie Hancock's 'Sound-System' (1984); their 'Village Life' duo album (1985) fused griot music and electronics.
Italian reed player Francesco Bearzatti recorded Monk'N'Roll in 2013 with Tinissima 4et, recasting Monk tunes with rock riffs and electric bass.
French vibraphonist Franck Tortiller recorded Early Down as a trio with bassist Yves Torchinsky and drummer David Pouradier Duteil in 2002.
Italian pianist Franco D'Andrea founded the Modern Art Trio in 1968 and played in jazz-rock band Perigeo from 1972-77, spanning free jazz and fusion.
Pianist Frank Kimbrough recorded Monk's Dreams with Scott Robinson, Rufus Reid and Billy Drummond, presenting the complete Monk repertoire across six CDs in 2018.
Alto saxophonist Frank Morgan recorded with Teddy Charles in 1953 and Kenny Clarke in 1954, led a GNP album in 1955 and resumed recording as a leader in 1985.
Drummer Frank Rosaly joined Giuseppe Doronzo and Andy Moor for Futuro Ancestrale, a trio performance recorded at Amsterdam's Bimhuis in June 2022.
Trombonist Frank Rosolino joined Stan Kenton's orchestra in late 1952, performed with Howard Rumsey's Lighthouse All-Stars in 1954-60 and toured with Benny Carter in 1974.
Tenor saxophonist Frank Socolow played in Boyd Raeburn's 1944 orchestra and Artie Shaw's 1949-50 band; his 1945 quintet session included Bud Powell.
Flutist and tenor saxophonist Frank Wess shaped Count Basie's 1953-64 'New Testament' band with lyrical flute solos that broadened big-band colors.
Tenor saxophonist Frank Wright emerged from Cleveland's free-jazz scene and recorded Frank Wright Trio (1965) and Your Prayer (1967) for ESP-Disk.
Drummer Franklin Kiermyer's 2014 quartet album Further pairs his drums with Azar Lawrence's tenor saxophone, Benito Gonzalez's piano and Juini Booth's bass.
Banjoist Fred Guy played on Duke Ellington's Washingtonians' 1927 Columbia East St. Louis Toodle-O and Victor Creole Love Call studio sessions.
Baritone saxophonist Fred Ho composed The Sweet Science Suite for his Green Monster Big Band in tribute to Muhammad Ali, with an expanded brass and reed lineup.
Cellist Fred Katz shaped the Chico Hamilton Quintet sound in 1955-1958 and made solo albums for Pacific Jazz, Decca and Warner Bros. before returning for a 1989 reunion.
Cellist Fred Lonberg-Holm added electronic effects and free improvisation to Ken Vandermark's Vandermark 5, joining the Chicago ensemble in 2005.
Belgian pianist Fred Van Hove played on Peter Brotzmann Octet's 'Machine Gun' (1968), joining Evan Parker, Peter Kowald and Han Bennink in free jazz.
Pianist Freddie Redd wrote the score to The Connection and performed in the play; Blue Note recorded his music in three sessions during 1960-1961.
Organist Freddie Roach played on Ike Quebec's Heavy Soul and It Might as Well Be Spring; he recorded Down to Earth for Blue Note in 1962 with Kenny Burrell.
Swedish reed player Fredrik Ljungkvist leads Yun Kan 5 and is a founding voice of the Scandinavian quintet Atomic, heard on Feet Music and Lucidity.
Norwegian alto saxophonist Frode Gjerstad recorded Bop Stop live in Cleveland on September 17, 2017 with Steve Swell, Jon Rune Strom and Paal Nilssen-Love.
Alto saxophonist Gary Bartz played with McCoy Tyner and Miles Davis, then formed Ntu Troop in 1970 to blend free jazz with soul, funk and African music.
Drummer and pianist Gary Husband led the fusion group Force Majeure on a March 2004 English tour with Randy Brecker, Jerry Goodman and Matthew Garrison.
Baritone saxophonist Gary Smulyan joined Woody Herman's Young Thundering Herd in 1978, then performed in the Mel Lewis Jazz Orchestra.
Luxembourg trumpeter and composer Gast Waltzing founded the jazz department of the Luxembourg Conservatory in 1986; recorded with Atmosphere and Life's Circle and scores films.
German reed player Gebhard Ullmann released Hemisphere 4 in 2023 with Liz Kosack, Silke Lange and Taiko Saito, using looping and electroacoustics.
Korean pianist Gee Hye Lee released Encounters in March 2025, joined by drummer Mareike Wiening, bassist Joel Locher and two horn guests.
Arranger-guitarist Gene Gifford joined the Orange Blossoms in 1929 and gave the renamed Casa Loma Orchestra its distinctive early swing charts.
Drummer (1909-1973) powered Benny Goodman's 1938 Carnegie Hall 'Sing, Sing, Sing'; his driving drum work made him a swing star. Later led his own big band.
Trumpeter, trombonist and arranger Gene Roland joined Stan Kenton in 1944, arranged Tampico in 1945 and later wrote extensively for Woody Herman.
American pianist Geoffrey Keezer contributes the opening track's piano part to Tim Garland's Songs to the North Sky, released by Edition in June 2014.
Austrian bassist Georg Breinschmid co-led the 2022 Berlin Philharmonic Mingus centenary concert and arranged Jelly Roll and Boogie Stop Shuffle.
Pianist-arranger George Handy worked with Boyd Raeburn in 1944-1946, wrote Tonsillectomy and Dalvatore Sally, and recorded his commissioned work The Bloos in 1946.
Trombonist and AACM composer George Lewis created 'Voyager' (1987), an interactive computer-improvisation system that plays alongside human jazz musicians.
Trombonist George Masso toured with Benny Goodman's sextet in 1973 after years of teaching and later led recording sessions for Famous Door and Dreamstreet.
Composer George Russell's 1953 Lydian Chromatic Concept helped open modal jazz; his 1956 'Jazz Workshop' featured Bill Evans and Art Farmer.
Bassist George Tucker recorded Horace Parlan's Us Three at Van Gelder Studio on April 20, 1960 and Speakin' My Piece with Tommy and Stanley Turrentine that July.
Bop pianist George Wallington played in Dizzy Gillespie's 1943-44 combo, wrote Lemon Drop and Godchild, and later led bands featuring Donald Byrd and Jackie McLean.
Chicago jazz drummer George Wettling worked in Artie Shaw's 1936 orchestra and led 1938 trio sessions with Bud Freeman and Jess Stacy before joining Eddie Condon.
Pianist Gerald Clayton released 'Bells On Sand' on Blue Note in 2022, featuring saxophonist Charles Lloyd and guest players John Clayton and Justin Brown.
Drummer Gerald Cleaver led the free-jazz quintet Black Host on 'Life in the Sugar Candle Mines' (2013) with Darius Jones, Cooper-Moore and Brandon Seabrook.
Pianist Gerald Wiggins toured with Louis Armstrong and Benny Carter in 1943, accompanied Lena Horne in 1950-51 and led a longstanding trio with Andy Simpkins and Paul Humphrey.
Arranger Gerald Wilson joined Jimmie Lunceford in 1939 and formed his own big band in 1944 with trombonist Melba Liston; his Pacific Jazz albums displayed innovative harmonies.
Salzburg-born percussionist Gerhard Laber (born 1946) moved from jazz drumming into experimental improvisation and sound art using unconventional instruments.
Drummer Gerry Hemingway formed BassDrumBone with Ray Anderson and Mark Helias; their trio recorded 'Oahspe' in November 1978 (released 1979).
Moldovan jazz vocalist Geta Burlacu recorded the ethno-jazz album 'Ce n-as da...' (2005), studied jazz in Chisinau and sang 'A Century of Love' at Eurovision 2008.
Italian trombonist Giancarlo Schiaffini recorded Deconstructing Monk in Africa with percussionist Sergio Armaroli in 2019 for a 2021 Dodicilune release.
Accordionist Gianni Coscia recorded Round About Weill with clarinetist Gianluigi Trovesi in Zurich in July 2004; ECM released the duo album in March 2005.
Sicilian saxophonist Gianni Gebbia joined The Mayfield with Heiner Goebbels, Camille Emaille and other improvisers for a Paris session recorded in January 2022.
Alto saxophonist and arranger Gigi Gryce wrote the jazz standard 'Minority' and co-led the Jazz Lab Quintet with trumpeter Donald Byrd in the 1950s.
Pianist Gil Coggins played on Miles Davis Blue Note sessions at WOR Studios in May 1952 and April 1953, with J.J. Johnson, Jackie McLean and Jimmy Heath.
Romanian violinist and bandleader Giorgi Vintilescu led Berlin's Palais de Danse Orchestra and recorded ragtime around 1912, before the swing era.
Multi-reedist Giuseppi Logan led an October 1964 Bell Studios session with Don Pullen, Eddie Gomez and Milford Graves for The Giuseppi Logan Quartet.
Italian pianist Glauco Venier recorded Miniatures in Lugano in December 2013, combining solo piano with gongs, bells and resonant sculptures.
Bassist Glen Moore recorded Oregon's 1983 ECM album with Ralph Towner, Paul McCandless and Collin Walcott, contributing the pieces Arianna and Skyline.
Cornetist Graham Haynes joined Marty Ehrlich and the Warriors of the Wonderful Sound for Muhal Richard Abrams's Soundpath, recorded in Philadelphia in 2018.
Soulful jazz guitarist (1935-1979). His 1963 'Idle Moments' session paired him with Joe Henderson, Bobby Hutcherson and Duke Pearson; hear also 'Jean de Fleur'.
Saxophonist Greg Abate played lead alto in Ray Charles's orchestra and tenor sax in the revived Artie Shaw Orchestra before recording as a leader.
Percussionist Gregg Bendian revisited Coltrane's Interstellar Space in a live duo with guitarist Nels Cline, recorded in 1998 in California and New York.
Drummer Gregory Hutchinson joined bassist Sylvain Romano in one of Jacky Terrasson's rotating trio lineups for the Blue Note album 53.
Algerian percussionist Guem supplied the recorded hand-percussion material heard on Razen's 2023 Hier l'An 4000 and composed on the release.
Argentine pianist Guillermo Klein led Los Guachos V, a 2016 Sunnyside release with Ben Monder, Chris Cheek, Miguel Zenon, Jeff Ballard and more.
Ghanaian drummer Guy Warren fused African percussion and jazz on Africa Speaks, America Answers, recorded in Chicago in 1956 with the Gene Esposito group.
Tenor saxophonist and hard-bop composer. His 1960 Blue Note album 'Soul Station' with Wynton Kelly, Paul Chambers and Art Blakey showcases his melodic, soulful improvising.
German pianist and composer Hannes Zerbe founded his Berlin Jazz Orchestra in 2011, combining improvised writing with modern orchestral influences.
Cuban pianist Harold Lopez-Nussa made his Blue Note debut with Timba a la Americana in 2023, working with Gregoire Maret, Luques Curtis and his brother Ruy.
Hard-bop pianist from Memphis worked with the Jazztet, Lionel Hampton and Lee Morgan. Recorded four leader albums for Prestige (1968-70) and later toured in piano ensembles.
Tenor saxophonist Harold Vick recorded his first leader album Steppin' Out! for Blue Note in 1963 and later recorded with Jack DeJohnette's group Compost in 1972.
Austrian Roma guitarist Harri Stojka leads the Harri Stojka Express, blending jazz improvisation with swing, blues, rock and Roma musical traditions.
Trombonist and arranger Harry Betts worked with Stan Kenton in the early 1950s and led the 1962 jazz album The Jazz Soul of Doctor Kildare.
Trumpeter Harry Sweets Edison played in Jeter-Pillars in 1933-1935, joined Count Basie in 1937 and later recorded behind singers Frank Sinatra and Billie Holiday.
Norwegian percussionist Helge Andreas Norbakken played alongside drummer Torstein Lofthus on Mathias Eick's Ravensburg, recorded in June 2017.
Alto saxophonist Herb Geller led a 1954-55 quartet with pianist Lorraine Geller and moved to Berlin in 1962 after playing on Los Angeles jazz sessions.
Flutist Herbie Mann's 'Memphis Underground' (1969) brought soul grooves into jazz with producer Tom Dowd and guitarist Sonny Sharrock.
Pianist Herbie Nichols made three Blue Note trio albums in 1955-1956; his May 1955 Prophetic sessions paired bassist Al McKibbon and drummer Art Blakey.
Jazz pianist Hiromi Uehara led Sonicbloom on 'Time Control' (2007), mixing dazzling keyboard improvisations with Dave Fiuczynski's electric guitar.
Canadian jazz vocalist Holly Cole recorded the Tom Waits songbook Temptation and teamed with pianist Aaron Davis on Dark Moon.
South African trumpeter Hugh Masekela (1939-2018) recorded 'Grazing in the Grass' (1968), played in the Jazz Epistles and toured with Paul Simon's Graceland band.
Trumpeter Ingrid Jensen won a Juno for her 1995 debut 'Vernal Fields'; 'Infinitude' paired her with sister Christine Jensen and Ben Monder.
Violinist and vocalist Irene Aebi played on Steve Lacy's The Condor with Steve Potts, Bobby Few, Jean-Jacques Avenel and Oliver Johnson, recorded in Milan in June 1985.
Jazz singer Irene Kral spent nine months with Maynard Ferguson's band in 1957 and made 1974-77 recordings including two intimate piano duets with Alan Broadbent.
Bassist Jack Bruce recorded the upright-bass jazz album 'Things We Like' in August 1968 with Jon Hiseman, Dick Heckstall-Smith and John McLaughlin.
Swing trombonist Jack Jenney organized his own big band in 1939 and soloed on Artie Shaw's Stardust while working with Shaw during 1940-1942.
Tenor saxophonist and arranger Jack Montrose joined the John Kirby Sextet in 1947 and made the 1955 Atlantic album Arranged/Played/Composed by Jack Montrose.
Paris-raised jazz pianist Jacky Terrasson won the 1993 Thelonious Monk piano competition, toured with Betty Carter and subsequently signed to Blue Note.
Danish guitarist Jakob Bro recorded Bay of Rainbows live in New York in July 2017 with Thomas Morgan on bass and Joey Baron on drums.
Pianist/composer (d. 1955) pioneered Harlem stride. Wrote 'The Charleston' for 'Runnin' Wild' (1923); recorded piano rolls and accompanied Bessie Smith in New York.
Norwegian tenor saxophonist Jan Garbarek recorded the free-jazz 'Afric Pepperbird' (1970; issued 1971) and later played in Keith Jarrett's European Quartet.
Soprano saxophonist Jane Ira Bloom composed NASA-commissioned 'Most Distant Galaxy' (1989) for saxophone, live electronics and percussion.
Pianist Jason Moran recorded 'Black Stars' (2001) with bassist Tarus Mateen, drummer Nasheet Waits and guest Sam Rivers, bringing free-jazz ideas into a trio.
Pianist Jason Rebello plays selected tracks on Tim Garland's 2014 Songs to the North Sky, sharing the keyboard role with John Turville and Geoffrey Keezer.
Japanese pianist and producer Ryota Nozaki created Jazztronik, releasing Samurai in February 2004 and Universal Language in 2021.
Experimental jazz vocalist heard on Carla Bley's 'Escalator Over the Hill' and Marion Brown's 'Afternoon of a Georgia Faun'; her work bridged voice and free improvisation.
Guitarist Jeff Parker's solo 'Forfolks' (2021) uses loops and improvisation to connect Chicago jazz guitar, minimalism and experimental electronics.
Jazz pianist, composer and bandleader; his Red Hot Peppers recorded in Chicago in 1926-27. His 1938 Library of Congress sessions preserved memories of early jazz.
Drummer Jim Black's AlasNoAxis quartet released 'Habyor' (2004), blending jazz improvisation with rock guitar energy and ambient electronics.
Alto saxophonist Jimmy Lyons supplied bebop-rooted lines to Cecil Taylor's free-jazz groups for more than two decades, including Unit Structures.
Pianist Jimmy Rowles played in Woody Herman's First Herd, backed Billie Holiday and Peggy Lee, and toured with Ella Fitzgerald from 1981 to 1983.
Drummer Jo Jones (1911-1985) anchored Count Basie's famed rhythm section with Freddie Green and Walter Page. His swinging pulse helped define the Basie band of the 1930s.
Reed player Joe Farrell recorded Outback for CTI in November 1971 with Chick Corea, Buster Williams, Elvin Jones and Airto Moreira.
Jazz violinist Joe Kennedy Jr. played on the 1949 Disc release Trends with Ahmad Jamal and made Strings by Candlelight in 1962 with Hank Jones and Kenny Burrell.
Tenor saxophonist Joe Lovano released 'Quartets: Live at the Village Vanguard' (1995), drawing on performances by two different quartets recorded in 1994-95.
Jazz guitarist Joe Pass (1929-1994) made the solo-guitar 'Virtuoso' series for Pablo Records; recorded with Ella Fitzgerald on 'Take Love Easy' and worked with Oscar Peterson.
Clarinetist John Carter composed Dauwhe for an octet including Bobby Bradford, James Newton, Red Callender and Roberto Miranda, recorded in Los Angeles in 1982.
Jazz bassist and arranger (born 1952) toured with Count Basie and helped found the Clayton-Hamilton Jazz Orchestra in 1986; recorded and arranged music with Diana Krall.
Tenor saxophonist (1931-1995), a central voice in Sun Ra's Arkestra from 1953. Recorded 'Blowing in from Chicago' with Clifford Jordan and also played with Art Blakey.
Drummer and percussionist John Hollenbeck joined Tony Malaby's Apparitions on Voladores with Drew Gress and Tom Rainey, expanding its percussion textures.
Bassist John Kirby led a polished six-piece swing band from 1937, nicknamed the 'Biggest Little Band in the Land'; its intricate charts helped shape chamber jazz.
English guitarist (born 1942) helped shape electric jazz fusion on Miles Davis's 'Bitches Brew'; founded Mahavishnu Orchestra and Shakti, linking jazz, rock and Indian rhythms.
Danish saxophonist co-founded the New York Art Quartet; appeared on Coltrane's 'Ascension' and Albert Ayler's 'New York Eye and Ear Control'; toured Europe with free-jazz groups.
Trumpeter Johnny Coles recorded 'Little Johnny C' (1963) with Joe Henderson and Duke Pearson, played with Gil Evans and joined Charles Mingus's 1964 touring sextet.
Jazz organist Johnny 'Hammond' Smith recorded for Prestige and Riverside before joining Milestone in 1975; on 'Forever Taurus' he explored electric piano and synthesizers.
Composer/arranger (1925-2020) wrote 'The Shadow of Your Smile', arranged Frank Sinatra's 'Ring-a-Ding-Ding!' and worked with Shirley Horn in jazz, pop and film.
Guitarist and banjoist Johnny St. Cyr played on Louis Armstrong's landmark Hot Five recordings, including 'Cornet Chop Suey' (1926) with Johnny Dodds and Lil Hardin.
Tenor saxophonist Joki Freund appears in the Jazz Ensemble des HR anthology Atmospheric Conditions Permitting, drawn from Frankfurt broadcasts of 1967-1993.
Dutch bassist Joris Teepe led For Adults Only, recorded live at Smalls in 1998 with Chris Potter, Don Braden, David Hazeltine and Bruce Cox; issued in 2000.
Brazilian pianist Jovino Santos Neto led his first Seattle quartet concert in April 1995 and later recorded a chamber duo with bassoonist Martin Kuuskmann.
Vocalist Judi Silvano released Lessons Learned in 2018 with her Zephyr Band and tenor saxophonist Joe Lovano, who also produced the album.
Trombonist Julian Priester recorded 'Love, Love' in 1973 after Herbie Hancock's Mwandishi band, fusing open jazz with synthesizers and funk.
Composer Julius Hemphill's saxophone-sextet music was sustained by Marty Ehrlich on Hard Blues, a live recording from Lisbon's Jazz em Agosto in 2003.
Percussionist Kahil El'Zabar founded Chicago's Ethnic Heritage Ensemble in 1974, joining AACM-influenced improvisation to African-rooted percussion.
Liberian-German electric bassist Kai Eckhardt recorded his 2014 leader album Zeitgeist in Berkeley and worked with Brazilian poet Regina Camargo on B-link.
Norwegian saxophonist and goat-horn player Karl Seglem blends Nordic folk instruments with jazz, issuing Ossicles in 2010 and Nordic Balm in 2017.
Bassist Kaveh Rastegar was part of Kneebody's five-piece 2007 Low Electrical Worker band and co-wrote Hearts Won't Break for 2019's Chapters.
Japanese pianist and composer Keiko Matsui released Euphoria in 2023 with guests including guitarist Mike Stern, trumpeter Randy Brecker and singer Lalah Hathaway.
Prepared-guitar improviser Keith Rowe recorded a live duo with percussionist Burkhard Beins in Berlin on May 13, 2004 for Erstwhile's ErstLive series.
Detroit jazz guitarist (born 1931) pioneered guitar-bass-drums trios; recorded 'Midnight Blue' (1963), played with John Coltrane and toured with Oscar Peterson.
Jazz pianist Kenny Drew Jr. played Thelonious Monk's 'In Walked Bud' on Marian McPartland's 'Piano Jazz' in 1992, alongside original composition 'Coral Sea'.
Canadian trumpeter and flugelhornist blended lyricism and free jazz. His 1975 New York recording 'Gnu High' paired him with Keith Jarrett, Dave Holland and Jack DeJohnette.
Bassist Kermit Driscoll recorded Bill Frisell Band's Lookout for Hope in March 1987 with Hank Roberts and Joey Baron, released by ECM in 1988.
Guitarist Kevin Eubanks recorded Dave Holland Quartet's Extensions in September 1989 and wrote its tracks Nemesis and Color of Mind.
Cornetist and bandleader whose Creole Jazz Band recorded 'Dippermouth Blues' in Richmond, Indiana, in 1923 with Louis Armstrong, Johnny Dodds and Lil Hardin.
Jazz guitarist Kurt Rosenwinkel fused electronics with acoustic interplay on 'Heartcore' (2003), recorded with Mark Turner and produced by hip-hop artist Q-Tip.
Pianist whose path ran from free jazz to fusion and hard bop. Recorded with Lee Morgan and Jackie McLean, joined Blood, Sweat & Tears in 1972 and Woody Shaw's quintet in 1986.
Organist Larry Young pushed Hammond B3 jazz beyond soul-jazz patterns: 'Unity' (1965) paired his modal post-bop with Woody Shaw, Joe Henderson and Elvin Jones.
Hong Kong-born improvising pianist Lee Pui Ming joined the Toronto Cluttertones on Leeways in 2018, adding piano and voice to their ensemble.
Trumpeter Lester Bowie helped define the Art Ensemble of Chicago's avant-garde jazz; hear 'Nice Guys' from the group's ECM sessions and his theme 'Charlie M'.
Tenor saxophonist (1909-1959) whose airy phrasing shaped swing. Featured with Count Basie's orchestra; hear 'Lester Leaps In' and 'Taxi War Dance'.
Vibraphonist Lionel Hampton joined Benny Goodman's quartet in 1936 and led his own big band. His 1942 hit 'Flying Home' featured Illinois Jacquet's tenor saxophone solo.
Beninese guitarist Lionel Loueke recorded HH in Italy in February 2019, interpreting Herbie Hancock compositions for the album released by Edition in October 2020.
American jazz multi-instrumentalist Lloyd Miller self-released Oriental Jazz in 1968, pairing modal approaches with Persian santur, oud and Turkish saz.
Danish saxophonist Lotte Anker recorded Life and Other Transient Storms live with Susana Santos Silva, Sten Sandell, Torbjorn Zetterberg and Jon Falt.
Hard-bop drummer Louis Hayes played on Horace Silver's '6 Pieces of Silver' (1956), then joined Cannonball Adderley and Oscar Peterson's bands.
Pianist and composer Lyle Mays played on the Pat Metheny Group's 1978 debut and co-wrote 'Phase Dance' and 'San Lorenzo'; his keyboards helped define the group's sound.
Welsh experimental singer Maggie Nicols improvised voice, piano and tap dance with percussionist Dan Johnson on the live album Contact, released in 2025.
Arranger Manny Albam (1922-2001) led an octet on RCA's 'Jazz Workshop' (1955), and wrote 'The Blues Is Everybody's Business' for a 1957 Coral album.
Pianist Marc Cary recorded Focus Trio Live 2009 with David Ewell and Sameer Gupta, offering jazz standards and his own pieces in a groove-centered trio format.
Guitarist Marc Ribot led Ceramic Dog on 'Party Intellectuals' (2008), fusing abrasive electric guitar, jazz improvisation and punk energy.
Pianist Marcin Wasilewski led his Polish trio with Slawomir Kurkiewicz and Michal Miskiewicz on Trio, recorded in Oslo in March 2004.
Bassist and producer Marcus Miller wrote and produced Miles Davis's album 'Tutu' (1986), and recorded with Aretha Franklin, George Benson and Al Jarreau.
Vibraphonist Margie Hyams played with Woody Herman's First Herd in 1944-45, led a trio in 1945-48 and joined George Shearing's original quintet in 1949.
Neapolitan vocalist Maria Pia De Vito translated Pergolesi's Stabat Mater into Neapolitan for Il Pergolese, an ECM quartet recording issued in 2013.
British-born pianist (1918-2013) played New York's Hickory House for eight years and hosted NPR's 'Piano Jazz' from 1979, pairing conversation with jazz duets.
Swiss electric bassist Marino Pliakas recorded Full Blast with Peter Brotzmann and Michael Wertmuller in Cologne in February 2006.
Double bassist Mario Pavone led the horn-rich Vertical sextet with Dave Ballou, Tony Malaby, Oscar Noriega, Peter McEachern and Mike Sarin in Brooklyn.
Italian alto and soprano saxophonist Mario Schiano played and sang with the Italian Instabile Orchestra in its December 1997 Pisa festival recording.
Cornetist Mark Charig recorded Boundaries with Elton Dean, Keith Tippett, Louis Moholo and Marcio Mattos in Ludwigsburg in February 1980.
Bassist Mark Dresser led the 2013 quintet album 'Nourishments', bringing extended double-bass techniques into tightly composed free improvisation.
Bassist Mark Helias joined Paul Dunmall, Tony Malaby and Kevin Norton on Ancient and Future Airs, an improvising quartet recorded after the 2008 Vision Festival.
British saxophonist Mark Lockheart released Shapeshifter in 2026 with bassist Huw V Williams and drummer Jay Davis, combining improvised jazz and ambient textures.
Ukrainian bassist Mark Tokar joined Lithuanian saxophonist Liudas Mockunas and drummer Arnas Mikalkenas for a live Lviv trio performance in April 2024.
Drummer Martin France joined Kenny Wheeler for Songs for Quintet, recorded in December 2013 at Abbey Road with Stan Sulzmann, John Parricelli and Chris Laurence.
Swedish pianist Martin Tingvall released PAX with Cuban bassist Omar Rodriguez Calvo and German drummer Jurgen Spiegel on SKIP Records in August 2025.
Multi-reedist Marty Ehrlich led Trio Exaltation with bassist John Hebert and drummer Nasheet Waits, presenting eight new originals and Andrew Hill's Dusk.
Drummer Marvin Smitty Smith recorded Dave Holland Quartet's Extensions at Power Station, New York, in September 1989 with Steve Coleman and Kevin Eubanks.
Vocalist Mary Ann McCall sang with Charlie Barnet in 1939-40 and Woody Herman's First and Second Herds, then recorded leader sessions for Columbia and Discovery.
Jazz guitarist Mary Osborne (1921-1992) was inspired by Charlie Christian; played with Joe Venuti and recorded alongside Mary Lou Williams and Coleman Hawkins in the 1940s.
Dutch jazz accordionist Mat Mathews pursued bebop-oriented playing after hearing Joe Mooney on radio and recorded The Modern Art of Jazz in 1956.
Alto saxophonist Matana Roberts recorded 'Coin Coin Chapter One' live in a Montreal studio in July 2010; the 2011 release blends voice and improvisation.
Swiss flugelhornist Matthieu Michel recorded Elina Duni's Lost Ships in February 2020 with Rob Luft and Fred Thomas, blending folk songs and jazz ballads.
Saxophonist-arranger Med Flory founded a New York band in 1954, moved west in 1956 and co-founded Supersax in 1972 to play Charlie Parker solos as ensemble parts.
Trombonist-arranger Melba Liston shaped Randy Weston's 'Little Niles' (1959) and later 'Khepera' (1998), expanding jazz orchestration.
Electric bassist Melvin Gibbs joined Ronald Shannon Jackson's Decoding Society on Eye on You, recorded February 1980 with Billy Bang, Bern Nix and Vernon Reid.
German jazz guitarist Michael Arlt toured and recorded with Red Holloway, Paquito D'Rivera and Houston Person; leads the organ trio We Three and teaches in Wurzburg.
Bassist Michael Bisio recorded the drummerless SKM trio album Three with tenor saxophonist Stephen Gauci and pianist Kris Davis in 2008.
Reed player Michael Moore contributed alto saxophone and clarinet to Sepk, an eclectic Orquesta del Tiempo Perdido album composed by Jeroen Kimman.
California-born percussionist Michael Vatcher moved to Amsterdam in 1981; played free improvisation with Michael Moore, John Zorn, Tristan Honsinger and The Ex.
Violinist Michael White recorded Pneuma with Edwin Kelly, Ray Drummond and Kenneth Nash in Los Angeles in July 1972 for the Impulse! label.
Drummer Michael Zerang joined Steve Swell, Gebhard Ullmann and Fred Lonberg-Holm for The Chicago Plan, recorded in Chicago in September 2015.
French pianist Michel Petrucciani recorded 'Power of Three' at Montreux in 1986 with guitarist Jim Hall; saxophonist Wayne Shorter joined for trio pieces.
Actor/singer Michelle Dockery formed Americana duo Michael & Michelle with Michael Fox. Their 2022 EP 'The Watching Silence' was preceded by single 'Calming Storm'.
Bassist Mick Hutton played on Martin Speake's Change of Heart with Bobo Stenson and Paul Motian, recorded at Rainbow Studio in Oslo in April 2002.
Alto saxophonist Mike Osborne recorded with the Mike Westbrook Concert Band on Love Songs in 1970 and the expanded Metropolis sessions in 1971.
Bassist Mike Richmond played acoustic and electric bass on Jack DeJohnette's Directions album Untitled, originally issued by ECM in September 1976.
Guitarist Mike Stern recorded Michael Mantler's Something There in 1982 with Carla Bley, Steve Swallow and Nick Mason plus London orchestral strings.
Pianist-composer Mike Westbrook led a large British jazz ensemble for Love Songs in 1970, featuring Norma Winstone, Mike Osborne and Chris Spedding.
Finnish saxophonist Mikko Innanen recorded 'Spring Odyssey' with Jaak Sooaar and Han Bennink; he also led the 10+ ensemble on 'GROTTO' (2016).
French percussionist Mino Cinelu guests on track four of Francis Jacob's Three Blind Mice album, alongside guest vocalist Melanie Dahan.
Japanese-American koto improviser Miya Masaoka joined harpist Zeena Parkins and pianist Myra Melford on MZM, recorded in 2014 and 2016.
Senegalese vocalist Mola Sylla sings and plays mbira and xalam on Requiem for a Dying Planet, the 2006 Ernst Reijseger film-music album.
South African trumpeter Mongezi Feza played in the Blue Notes' final 1964 homeland concerts with Chris McGregor and Dudu Pukwana, later issued as Legacy.
South African saxophonist Morris Goldberg recorded Ojoyo Plays Safrojazz with trumpeter Chris Botti, bassist Bakithi Kumalo and drummer Anton Fig.
Norwegian pianist Morten Gunnar Larsen played ragtime and New Orleans music on a 2019 Danish concert tour with Norbert Susemihl's Joyful Gumbo.
Japanese free bassist Motoharu Yoshizawa recorded Way of the Breeze with Korean percussionist Kim Dae Hwan in Hofu in September 1993.
Japanese drummer Motohiko Hino recorded TOKO live at Nemu no Sato in July 1975 with guitarist Kazumi Watanabe and bassist Isao Suzuki.
Pianist Myra Melford's Fire and Water Quintet recorded 'For the Love of Fire and Water' (2022) with Mary Halvorson, Tomeka Reid and Susie Ibarra.
Scat-focused jazz vocalist Nancy King made the 2006 duo album 'Live at Jazz Standard' with pianist Fred Hersch; she also worked with Glen Moore.
Drummer Nasheet Waits recorded Baida at Avatar Studios in October 2012 with Ralph Alessi, Jason Moran and Drew Gress; ECM issued the album in 2013.
Pianist-arranger Nat Pierce played with Woody Herman's Third Herd from 1951 to 1955, arranged the 1957 Sound of Jazz telecast and co-led the Capp-Pierce Juggernaut.
Guitarist Nate Radley joined pianist Kris Davis and the Infrasound octet on Save Your Breath, mixing electric guitar and organ with four clarinets.
Belgian pianist Nathalie Loriers recorded Nympheas in 1991 with Kurt van Herck, Philippe Aerts and Mimi Verderame, later forming a trio with Postma and Thys.
Saxophonist and flutist Nathan Davis recorded Happy Girl in 1965 with Woody Shaw, Larry Young, Jimmy Woode and Billy Brooks; he composed The Flute in the Blues.
Japanese trumpeter Natsuki Tamura recorded the freely improvised duo 'How Many?' with pianist Satoko Fujii and played in her big-band album 'South Wind' (1997).
New Orleans trumpeter Natty Dominique recorded with Jelly Roll Morton in 1923 and frequently worked with clarinetist Johnny Dodds, recording with him into 1940.
Brazilian guitarist (born 1977) blends classical technique and jazz; played with Pat Metheny and Michel Petrucciani, and recorded for Label Bleu with Magic Malik in 2003.
Flutist Nicole Mitchell played on Mark Dresser Seven's Ain't Nothing But a Cyber Coup & You with Marty Ehrlich, Jim Black and an expanded horn-and-strings group.
Tenor saxophonist Nikele Moyake helped form Cape Town's multiracial Blue Notes with Chris McGregor, Dudu Pukwana, Mongezi Feza, Johnny Dyani and Louis Moholo-Moholo.
Norwegian guitarist and vocalist Nils-Olav Johansen joined Cecilie Grundt Quintet at Dokkhuset in March 2019 on guitar, banjo and voice.
Free-jazz alto saxophonist Noah Howard led 'The Black Ark' (1969), a fiery ensemble with Arthur Doyle, Muhammad Ali and bassist Sirone.
Singer-bandleader Noble Sissle collaborated with Eubie Blake on the 1921 Broadway musical Shuffle Along and later led an orchestra that featured Lena Horne.
British jazz vocalist Norma Winstone recorded Descansado in March 2017 with Klaus Gesing, Glauco Venier and guests Norbakken and Brunello.
Turkish percussionist Okay Temiz played on Don Cherry's Dona Nostra, recorded in Oslo in March 1993 with Bobo Stenson and Lennart Aberg.
Russian-born Norwegian jazz pianist Olga Konkova recorded the piano-guitar duo December Songs with Jens Thoresen, originally issued in 2017.
German pianist and vocalist Olivia Trummer recorded Fly Now in New York and Berlin in 2013 with bassist Matt Penman and guest Kurt Rosenwinkel.
Israeli bassist Omer Avital formed Qantar in 2016 and released its self-titled quintet album in 2018 with two saxophones, piano and drums.
Clarinetist Omer Simeon recorded with Jelly Roll Morton in 1926 and 1928, then played in Earl Hines's big band and Wilbur DeParis's New Orleans ensemble.
Venezuelan conga player Orlando Poleo performs on Paoli Mejias's 2025 PAPOLEO, adding quitipla and congas to the Latin-jazz arrangement.
Steel-pan player Othello Molineaux recorded Opus Pocus on Jaco Pastorius' 1976 solo debut and Liberty City on Word of Mouth, issued in 1981.
Japanese guitarist Otomo Yoshihide led Ground-Zero's 'Consume Red' (1997), building collective noise improvisation around sampled traditional Korean music.
Alto saxophonist Otto Hardwick was an early Duke Ellington colleague, left the orchestra in 1928, returned in 1932 and stayed until 1946.
German pianist Pablo Held expanded his trio into a ten-piece ensemble for GLOW, recording the sessions in March 2010 for a February 2011 release.
Guitarist Pat Martino's leader debut 'El Hombre' (1967) featured Trudy Pitts on organ and Latin percussion, an early soul-jazz guitar statement.
Seattle pianist Patti Bown joined Quincy Jones's 1959 European big-band tour for Free and Easy; she also recorded with Gene Ammons and accompanied Dinah Washington.
Drummer Paul Barbarin wrote New Orleans standard 'Bourbon Street Parade'; his Atlantic recording of January 1955 pairs parade rhythm with jazz improvisation.
Alto saxophonist Paul Desmond composed 'Take Five' for the Dave Brubeck Quartet's 1959 'Time Out' album, a celebrated experiment in unusual jazz meters.
Saxophonist Paul Dunmall led an octet on Bridging, recorded live at the Jazz em Agosto festival with Keith Tippett, Paul Rutherford and other improvisers.
Percussionist Paul Lytton recorded Some Other Season with violinist Philipp Wachsmann in Winterthur in October 1997, and ECM issued the duo in 1999.
Oboist and reed player Paul McCandless explored global sounds in Oregon. The quartet's 1983 ECM album paired him with Ralph Towner, Collin Walcott and Glen Moore.
Trombonist Paul Rutherford joined Paul Dunmall's Bridging octet with Keith Tippett, Gethin Liddington and Tony Levin for a live Jazz em Agosto recording.
Jazz vocalist and songwriter Peggy Lee recorded 'Why Don't You Do Right?' (1942) with Benny Goodman's orchestra; she also wrote and produced her own songs.
German jazz bassist Pepe Berns (born 1966) played the 1991 Malta Jazzfest and studied with Charlie Haden; performed in New York with Eliot Zigmund and Ben Monder.
Baritone saxophonist Pepper Adams worked with Kenny Burrell and Paul Chambers in 1955, moved to New York in 1956 and began extensive recording with Donald Byrd in 1958.
Swedish free-jazz pianist Per Henrik Wallin recorded his final solo album Velodromer across two sessions in 2004 and 2005.
Norwegian bassist Per Zanussi led the three-saxophone quintet Zanussi Five, whose self-titled debut appeared in February 2005.
Bassist Percy Jones joined Shankar and Caroline on The Epidemics, a 1985 studio session featuring 10-string double violin and electronic textures.
West Coast pianist Pete Jolly joined Shorty Rogers's quintet in 1954 and recorded 'Jolly Jumps In' for RCA in 1955 with Shelly Manne and Curtis Counce.
Drummer Pete La Roca led 'Basra' (Blue Note, 1965) with Joe Henderson, Steve Kuhn and Steve Swallow, exploring modal colors inside hard bop.
Dutch pianist Peter Beets recorded New York Trio - Page Two in Brooklyn on Dec. 16, 2002 with bassist Larry Grenadier and drummer Willie Jones III; released in 2003.
Drummer Phil Collins joined jazz-fusion group Brand X in 1975, playing alongside John Goodsall, Percy Jones and Robin Lumley on 1976 album 'Unorthodox Behaviour'.
Belgian guitarist Philip Catherine joined Jean-Luc Ponty's quintet in 1971 and released 'September Man' in 1974, crossing swing and fusion.
Swiss jazz guitarist Philipp Schaufelberger played Kenny Wheeler's Banff Jazz Orchestra and toured with Harald Haerter's quartet, including sets with Dewey Redman.
Belgian bassist Philippe Aerts led the quartet recording Back to the Old World in 2002 with Bert Joris, John Ruocco and drummer Tony Levin.
French electric guitarist Philippe Deschepper recorded MMXXIV AD in Zurich in May 2024 with fellow improvising guitarist Noel Akchote.
French bassist Pierre Michelot played on Miles Davis's improvised 'Ascenseur pour l'echafaud' film score (Paris, December 1957) with Kenny Clarke.
Jazz multi-reed player Rahsaan Roland Kirk used circular breathing and sometimes played several horns simultaneously; he also performed with Charles Mingus.
Oregon co-founder Ralph Towner recorded solo classical-guitar album At First Light in Lugano in February 2022 for ECM release in March 2023.
Chicago pianist Ramsey Lewis (1935-2022) blended gospel and jazz; his trio's hit 'The In Crowd' (1965) was recorded live at Bohemian Caverns in Washington, DC.
Philadelphia trumpeter (born 1945) played with Horace Silver and Art Blakey, co-founded the jazz-rock group Dreams and recorded 'Score' (1968) with brother Michael.
Congolese pianist Ray Lema recorded the 2016 two-piano album Riddles with Laurent de Wilde and returned to Kinshasa for a Franco Luambo tribute in 2019.
Trumpeter and violinist Ray Nance joined Duke Ellington after work with Earl Hines and Horace Henderson; he soloed on the original Take the A Train.
Pianist Renee Rosnes recorded as a Blue Note leader from 1990 and became music director of ARTEMIS, whose debut Blue Note album arrived in 2020.
Cameroonian bassist and vocalist Richard Bona folds African melody into jazz and Afropop; his collaborations include Pat Metheny and Herbie Hancock.
Alto saxophonist Richie Cole popularized fast, playful bebop as 'Alto Madness', toured for four years with vocalist Eddie Jefferson and recorded with Phil Woods.
Italian pianist Rita Marcotulli joined Andy Sheppard and Michel Benita on the trio album Salt Catchers, recorded in Lugano in March 2025.
Trombonist Robin Eubanks recorded Dave Holland Quintet's The Razor's Edge in February 1987 with Steve Coleman, Kenny Wheeler and Marvin Smith.
Austrian vibraphonist Roland Neffe leads the jazz ensemble Vibes Beyond and Wood & Steel Trio; studied with Gary Burton and teaches jazz vibraphone in Nuremberg.
Drummer Ronald Shannon Jackson led the Decoding Society on Eye on You, recorded in New York in February 1980 with Billy Bang and Vernon Reid.
Sicilian trumpeter Roy Paci joined The Ex and Brass Unbound on Enormous Door in 2013 and recorded with Nigerian singer Chris Obehi.
Tenor saxophonist Rusty Bryant began leading Columbus bands in 1951 and returned to recording in 1968 with Groove Holmes before a series of Prestige albums.
Alto saxophonist Sahib Shihab recorded with Thelonious Monk, Milt Jackson, Al McKibbon and Art Blakey for Blue Note at WOR Studios on July 23, 1951.
Bassist Sam Jones composed 'Unit 7' with Cannonball Adderley; his 1960 Riverside album 'The Soul Society' also featured his jazz cello.
Pianist/composer Satoko Fujii led the 1997 'South Wind' big band, using intricate written passages and fiery free improvisation with trumpeter Natsuki Tamura.
Ragtime pianist/composer (c.1868-1917), a jazz precursor. Published 'Maple Leaf Rag' (1899) in Sedalia and wrote 'The Entertainer' and the opera 'Treemonisha'.
Italian trombonist Sebi Tramontana played in the December 1997 Italian Instabile Orchestra festival set and co-led Canzone a Due.
Philadelphia saxophonist Shafi Hadi, formerly Curtis Porter, played alto and tenor on Charles Mingus albums The Clown and New Tijuana Moods in the late 1950s.
Singer-pianist Shirley Horn recorded Embers and Ashes in 1960, opened for Miles Davis at the Village Vanguard and reunited with him on You Won't Forget Me in 1990.
South African singer Sibongile Khumalo released Ancient Evenings in 1996 and Live at the Market Theatre in 1998, blending African song and jazz.
New Orleans clarinetist and soprano saxophonist (1897-1959), known for expressive vibrato. Hear 'Summertime'; toured Europe with Will Marion Cook and later lived in France.
Norwegian vocalist Silje Nergaard joined Espen Berg Trio on the Paul Simon song I'd Do It For Your Love, released in March 2022.
Bassist Sirone joined Charles Gayle and Gerald Cleaver for the studio trio release Shout, pairing exploratory tenor saxophone with agile acoustic rhythm.
Brazilian accordionist Sivuca worked with Miriam Makeba as guitarist and bandleader and recorded a 1984 accordion duo with Chiquinho do Acordeom.
Trumpeter Snooky Young played lead with Jimmie Lunceford in 1939-42, helped found the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra in 1966 and joined The Tonight Show band.
Norwegian vocalist Solveig Slettahjell contributed to Jon Balke's Batagraf album Statements, made during 2003-04 and released by ECM in 2005.
Pianist and bandleader Stan Kenton recorded 'Artistry in Rhythm' for Capitol in November 1943; his orchestra later explored modern jazz with arranger Pete Rugolo.
British pianist Stan Tracey led the 1965 Under Milk Wood quartet with Bobby Wellins, Jeff Clyne and drummer Jackie Dougan after backing guests at Ronnie Scott's.
Pianist Stanley Cowell recorded Illusion Suite with Stanley Clarke and Jimmy Hopps in New York in November 1972; its original release followed in 1973.
Improviser Steve Beresford supplied electronics to Simon H. Fell's large-ensemble work Positions & Descriptions alongside Tim Berne and Rhodri Davies.
Pianist Steve Kuhn played in John Coltrane's quartet in 1960; his ECM trio album 'Wisteria' (2012) united Steve Swallow and Joey Baron.
Vibraphonist Steve Nelson recorded Dave Holland Quintet's Points of View in September 1997, alternating vibes and marimba in the new band.
Bassist Steve Rodby recorded First Circle with the Pat Metheny Group at New York's Power Station in February 1984 alongside Lyle Mays.
Trombonist Steve Turre recorded Avant Pop with Lester Bowie's Brass Fantasy at Tonstudio Bauer in March 1986 and contributed two compositions.
German-born Amsterdam saxophonist Susanne Alt recorded Royalty for Real in New York with James Hurt, Gerald Cannon and Willie Jones III.
Bandleader Teddy Hill led a successful 1930s swing orchestra and later managed Harlem's Minton's Playhouse, where after-hours jam sessions fostered early bebop.
Trumpeter Terence Blanchard recorded the Herbie Hancock-produced Flow in 2005 and led Magnetic in 2013, featuring Ron Carter and Lionel Loueke.
Trumpeter Terumasa Hino recorded 'Taro's Mood' in June 1973 with pianist Mikio Masuda, bassist Yoshio Ikeda and drummer Motohiko Hino.
Trumpeter and arranger Thad Jones co-founded the Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra in 1966; his modern big-band charts were heard on Mondays at the Village Vanguard.
Horace Silver's hard-bop quintet recorded '6 Pieces of Silver' (1956) for Blue Note; 'Senor Blues' featured Donald Byrd, Hank Mobley, Doug Watkins and Louis Hayes.
Pianist Oscar Peterson's trio with Herb Ellis on guitar and Ray Brown on bass recorded live at the Stratford Shakespearean Festival in 1956; hear 'Noreen's Nocturne'.
Austrian trumpeter Thomas Gansch co-founded Mnozil Brass and played in Vienna Art Orchestra (1998-2006); also leads jazz quintets and teaches trumpet in Vienna.
Norwegian guitarist Thomas T Dahl joined Mats Eilertsen's septet for Rubicon, recorded at Rainbow Studio in Oslo in May 2015.
Armenian jazz pianist Tigran Hamasyan's 'Mockroot' (2015) mixes Armenian folk songs, intricate jazz rhythms, rock, voice and electronic textures.
Alto saxophonist Tim Berne recorded 'Snakeoil' for ECM in 2011; the 2012 quartet album features Oscar Noriega, Matt Mitchell and Ches Smith in chamber-like free jazz.
British reed player Tim Garland released Songs to the North Sky in 2014, combining saxophones and bass clarinet with strings, piano and percussion.
Tenor saxophonist Tina Brooks recorded Minor Move in 1958 with Lee Morgan, Sonny Clark, Doug Watkins and Art Blakey; the hard-bop album was unreleased until 1980.
Drummer-composer Tom Skinner released Voices of Bishara in November 2022 with Nubya Garcia, Shabaka Hutchings, Tom Herbert and Kareem Dayes.
Swing trombonist Tommy Dorsey's orchestra paired Sy Oliver's hot arrangements with the 1940 debut of vocalist Frank Sinatra; hear 'Opus One'.
Hard-bop trumpeter Tommy Turrentine led a Time Records session in New York on January 19, 1960 with Stanley Turrentine, Horace Parlan and Max Roach.
Australian drummer Tony Buck co-founded improvised-music trio The Necks with Chris Abrahams and Lloyd Swanton in 1986; its hypnotic music unfolds slowly.
Bassist Tony Levin's jazz credits include Buddy Rich, Gary Burton and Steps Ahead; his Chapman Stick work also shaped progressive jazz-rock projects.
Brazilian guitarist and singer Toquinho (born 1946) partnered with poet Vinicius de Moraes on songs such as 'Tarde em Itapoa'; his solo repertoire includes 'Aquarela'.
Japanese jazz/hip-hop producer Uyama Hiroto collaborated with Nujabes and released 'A Son of the Sun' (2008), later establishing roph recordings and exploring free jazz.
Trumpeter-vocalist Valaida Snow appeared in the 1924 revue The Chocolate Dandies and led Chicago's Sunset Cafe bill in 1928 while touring widely as a performer.
Hungarian singer Veronika Harcsa recorded Lampafeny in Budapest in January 2011 with pianist Attila Blaho and guitarist Balint Gyemant.
Actor and improvisational musician Viggo Mortensen recorded with guitarist Buckethead; their experimental album 'One Less Thing to Worry About' appeared in 1997.
French horn player Vincent Chancey joined Lester Bowie's nine-piece Brass Fantasy for Avant Pop, recorded at Tonstudio Bauer in March 1986.
German guitarist Volker Kriegel features on ECM's Atmospheric Conditions Permitting, a Hessischer Rundfunk jazz-ensemble collection spanning 1967 to 1993.
Pianist Wade Legge joined Dizzy Gillespie after being heard as a bassist by Milt Jackson; he later recorded with Sonny Rollins and Charles Mingus.
Percussionist Warren Smith recorded on Enrico Rava's Quotation Marks, an adventurous album with Jeanne Lee, John Abercrombie and Jack DeJohnette.
Drummer Whit Dickey recorded the cornet-drums duo Fierce Silence with Kirk Knuffke in Brooklyn on October 14, 2015.
Bassist Wilbur Ware anchored Thelonious Monk's 1957 groups with John Coltrane and played Sonny Rollins's 'A Night at the Village Vanguard' sessions.
Trumpeter Frankie Newton backed Billie Holiday's April 1939 Commodore recordings of 'Strange Fruit' and 'Fine and Mellow' in his Cafe Society Orchestra.
South African tenor saxophonist Winston Mankunku Ngozi recorded Yakhal' Inkomo in 1968 with Lionel Pillay, Agrippa Magwaza and Early Mabuza.
Guitarist Wolfgang Muthspiel led ECM's 'Rising Grace' (2016) with Ambrose Akinmusire, Brad Mehldau, Larry Grenadier and Brian Blade.
Austrian reed player Wolfgang Puschnig recorded with Red Sun and Korean percussion group SamulNori in Seoul in May 1993 for ECM's White Tiger.
Trombonist Wolter Wierbos played at Jazzfest Berlin in 2016 with Alexander von Schlippenbach's Globe Unity Orchestra for its fiftieth anniversary.
Clarinetist and bandleader Woody Herman's orchestra recorded Jimmy Giuffre's 'Four Brothers' in Hollywood (1947), featuring Stan Getz, Zoot Sims and Serge Chaloff.
Trumpeter Woody Shaw (1944-1989) broadened modern jazz harmony; recorded 'Unity' with Larry Young (1965) and led the album 'Rosewood' (1977).
Pianist Wynton Kelly recorded fourteen Blue Note trio tracks in 1951, played with Miles Davis from 1959 to 1963 and then formed a trio with Paul Chambers and Jimmy Cobb.
Jazz pianist Yaron Herman released the Blue Note album 'Everyday' (2015) with drummer Ziv Ravitz, linking solo piano and percussive textures.
Composer Yoko Kanno leads the Seatbelts, whose 1998 'Cowboy Bebop' soundtrack mixed big-band jazz, blues and rock; she composed and arranged the theme 'Tank!'.
Saxophonist and flutist (1920-2013) brought global timbres to jazz; played with Dizzy Gillespie and Cannonball Adderley. Hear 'Eastern Sounds' (1961); toured Europe and Japan.
Polish violinist Zbigniew Seifert recorded Man of the Light with Joachim Kuhn, Cecil McBee and Billy Hart in 1976; MPS released the album in 1977.
Electric-harp improviser Zeena Parkins formed Phantom Orchard with electronic musician Ikue Mori, recording their self-titled 2004 album.
South African reed player Zim Ngqawana released four Sheer Sound studio albums: Zimology, Ingoma, Zimphonic Suites and Vadzimu.
New Orleans drummer Zutty Singleton played on Louis Armstrong's 1928 Hot Five 'Knee Drops' and 'West End Blues' era sessions with Earl Hines.
